## Journal With Each Hand

Lucia Capacchione, an art therapist, has been teaching this one for decades (it's in her book [Recovery of Your Inner Child](https://www.luciac.com/)). Write with your non-dominant hand, the clumsy one, whose letters already look like a first grader's, and let it put down whatever scared or hurt feelings are really there, nothing made up. Then your usual hand writes back as the grown-up. If talking to your little one or picturing them gets you only silence, this can get past it. And if the protective part grabs the pen first? It gets the clumsy hand until it's had its say.

If thinking things through on paper leaves you more confused, a simpler memory aid is fine. It keeps track of things without you having to work out what they mean at the same time. Looking for patterns can come later, if it's useful at all. A memory aid doesn't have to explain your life. It could be a short note of what happened, with the date, or a note of what helped. A reminder or a next step works too. Or you can leave yourself a voice note.
t71bb_secoiq:
## One Intention in the Morning, One Review at Night

The night half of this is a lot like the [Examen](https://www.ignatianspirituality.com/ignatian-prayer/the-examen/), the evening review Jesuits have done for centuries, just aimed at hooks. Mornings, pick one small intention, like "Today I'll notice one hook before I act on it." At night, look back over the day. Where did you catch the hook, and where did it run its routine anyway? Then what's the next small repair, or something that'd protect your little one?

And what good did you get today? Count the small stuff, like a warm moment, or some nerve you didn't know you had. Noticing the hook counts too, and it counts if you're only seeing it now, in the review. Same if you broke the pattern somewhere. Then repair what you can, and that's the day. Same intention tomorrow. Bed.
t71bb_secjll:
## Just Like Me

This one works best on a steadier day, when thinking about other people won't pull you out of your own shoes. Name the feeling plainly. Lonely, say. Then think of how many people are feeling that exact thing right now, and wanting it to stop, just like you. Some of them make it worse trying to get away from it. Just like you, sometimes. 😅 Wish all of you, you first, enough support to stay with it, so the pain stops with you.

If you've tried Pema Chödrön's [tonglen](https://www.lionsroar.com/how-to-practice-tonglen-meditation/), this is a gentler cousin, and normal breathing is fine. Whoever hurt you might come to mind, too. Forgiving them isn't part of it, and neither is picturing their childhood. Getting in touch is a separate decision, for a much calmer day, if it ever comes. With that many people feeling the same thing, the theory that you're the defective one gets kind of hard to keep up.
